name: Restaurant, café or bar
description: A restaurant, café, bistro or bar: the food and drink menu, events such as tastings or live music and guests' questions, with facts about table reservations, the cuisine, the price range, outdoor seating, takeaway and dietary options.

questions.question: Can guests reserve a table online? Give the address of the reservation page.
questions.help: The reservation button leads here. Leave it empty if guests reserve by phone – the button then calls the number from Business details – or if you do not take reservations.

questions.question: What kind of food and drink do you serve?
questions.help: In a few words, as guests would search for it, e.g. "Neapolitan pizza and natural wine" or "speciality coffee and homemade cakes".

questions.question: How would you state your price range?
questions.help: For example "mains 14–26 EUR" or "€€". Search engines show it next to your name, so keep it in line with the menu.

questions.question: Do you have a terrace, garden or other outdoor seating?
questions.help: For example "terrace with 30 seats, May to September". Leave it empty if there is none.

questions.question: Can guests in a wheelchair or with a pram get in, and is there an accessible toilet?
questions.help: Describe it as it is, e.g. "one step at the entrance, ramp on request, no accessible toilet" – an honest answer saves guests a wasted trip.

questions.question: Do you offer takeaway or delivery? How do guests order?
questions.help: For example "takeaway by phone, delivery through a delivery app". Leave it empty if you do neither.

questions.question: What do you offer for vegetarians, vegans and guests with allergies or intolerances?
questions.help: Only what the kitchen really does, e.g. "vegan dishes every day, gluten-free pasta on request". The labels of single dishes belong in the menu.

questions.question: Do you host private parties, groups or company events? For how many guests?
questions.help: For example "separate room for up to 40 guests, set menus on request". Leave it empty if you do not.

audit.message: Put your menu on the site as dishes with prices – guests decide by the menu, and a photo or PDF of it is hard to read on a phone.
The menu has not changed for half a year – check that the dishes, prices and allergens are still right.
Add your opening hours in Business details – guests check whether you are open before anything else.
Add your address in Business details – guests navigate by it and search engines put you on the map.
Say what kind of food you serve – it is what guests search for.
Say whether guests in a wheelchair or with a pram can get in – they need to know before they come.

claude: Guests decide in seconds: what kind of food, is it open now, what does it cost, can I book and where is it – put the opening hours ({{hours.status}}), the menu, a reservation button and the address at the top of the home page. The reservation button links to {{fact.reservation_url}}, or to tel:{{fact.company_phone}} when it is empty. The menu is the menu collection, never only a photo or PDF: keep it current, hide dishes that are off instead of deleting them, and change prices only when the owner gives them. Never guess allergens, ingredients, diet labels or prices – ask the owner; allergen labelling rules differ by country, so say they should be checked rather than stating them as law. Do not invent dishes, chefs, awards, ratings, reviews or guests' quotes, and avoid empty superlatives such as "the best in town" – describe the food with appetite but honestly.
